When dereferencing properties from potentially missing or malformed input artifacts, we should use `Array.isArray` to safely default to an empty array. Spreading a non-iterable (such as `null` or a non-array object) will throw a `TypeError` and crash the script.

```suggestion
  const reviewBacklogIds = Array.isArray(inputs.scheduledLayer?.deferrals?.review_backlog?.question_row_ids) ? inputs.scheduledLayer.deferrals.review_backlog.question_row_ids : [];
  const visualEvidenceIds = Array.isArray(inputs.scheduledLayer?.deferrals?.visual_evidence?.question_row_ids) ? inputs.scheduledLayer.deferrals.visual_evidence.question_row_ids : [];
  const blockedQuestionIds = sortedUnique([
    ...reviewBacklogIds,
    ...visualEvidenceIds,
  ]);
```

When writing unit tests for package validators, we should explicitly assert that all expected checks are present, pass, and are emitted in strict byte-order by ID to align with the repository's general rules.

```javascript
    const expectedCheckIds = [
      'accepted_and_provisional_layers_non_empty',
      'backlog_priority_queues_present',
      'coverage_report_counts_explicit',
      'high_risk_review_only',
      'no_credential_like_serialization',
      'no_forbidden_side_effects',
      'review_backlog_non_blocking',
      'safe_consumption_manifest_excludes_backlog_layers',
      'upstream_inputs_loaded_and_validator_backed',
    ];
    const actualCheckIds = result.validatorResult.checks.map((check) => check.id);
    expect(actualCheckIds).toEqual(expectedCheckIds);
    expect(result.validatorResult.checks.every((check) => check.status === 'pass')).toBe(true);
```

Fixed in 2e7a16a93. The validator test now asserts the exact expected check IDs in byte-order and verifies every emitted check passes.
